metadata.title: Gated exciton fluids III: a matrix-free Newton-Krylov solver and a 64x64 case it does not converge, and a classical node-arrangement study of shaped containers with the Fenris-CMRR engine
metadata.description: Third paper of the gated-exciton line (I: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23294615; II: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23297479). Two pre-registered work packages, each with a failed or partly failed gate, each re-checked by an independent hostile verifier. (1) A matrix-free Newton-Krylov solver (L-stable SDIRK2, GMRES, Fourier-diagonal block preconditioner, analytic Jacobian-vector products) for the driven-dissipative exciton Gross-Pitaevskii model with an incoherent reservoir: reproduces the dense-CVODE records and an independent reviewer's printed digits, second order in time, CPU cost per transient time unit growing like M^2.15 between 8x8 and 64x64 grids; slower than dense CVODE at 8x8 and faster at 16x16 (one transient, one seed). The registered 64x64 stationary-state gate at gate amplitude V0=0.5 is NOT MET: the run does not converge and shows a persistent pulsation of period about 970 at three resolutions, not tested with an independent integrator. The preconditioner planted-bug gate passed only in a regime where it could not fail, and a regime test failed for two of six variants. (2) A classical relaxation study with the Fenris-CMRR engine and the gated kernel in eleven shaped containers: the registered design (wall nodes at the mean spacing, uniform starts) did not confine the free nodes and was replaced by a half-spaced wall and random-sequential-addition starts; with that wall model the defect count depends strongly on the container shape (about 6 to about 30 non-sixfold nodes at N about 100) and less, but not negligibly in mid-range shapes, on the kernel; a concentration of defects at the wall was not demonstrated against a density null, and the statistics are thin. A classical design target, not an exciton prediction. No comparison with experimental data. Written by an AI system; checked by independent instances; not refereed.
metadata.notes: Standalone paper of the SocrateAI-Scientific-QuantumFluids programme, written by an AI system under the author's standing instructions.
